item.title: These Mini Backpacks Hold More Than You Think
item.description:
Source: Condé Nast Traveler
We love a hands-free life. From automatic doors to voice-activated everything, weâve spent a surprising amount of time figuring out how to do things without having to touch or hold anything. And thereâs arguably no product more iconic and enduring in its pursuit of hands-free convenience than the mighty backpackâwell, except maybe the mini version, which offers the same convenience in a lighter, more travel-friendly package. I recently returned from a hiking trip through the Dolomites where the medium version of the Janji Revy Pack was the workhorse of my six-hour days (a claim my very sore legs would like to have a word with). The lighter pack kept me moving freely without the bulk of a traditional backpack weighing me down, allowing me to reserve my energy for the trail ahead. Since then, Iâve found myself reaching for even smaller backpacks more often, particularly for travel days, adventures outdoors, and as the perfect in-flight carry-on for my toddler. These mini packs give you the practicality of a regular backpack without the temptation of carrying more than you may actually use, striking that sweet spot between packing what you need and what you want just in case. Here are 11 of the best mini backpacks for travel, from creatively bold designs to minimalist-chic options, all offering a balance of organization and comfort that keep your essentials close and your hands free.

item.title: Capital One Venture X Business offers up to 300,000 bonus miles and a $1,000 travel credit
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy
Capital One Venture X Business offers up to 300,000 bonus miles and a $1,000 travel credit If you're a high-spending business owner who loves to travel, Capital One is offering a valuable bonus on a top-tier travel rewards card. The current offer on the Capital One Venture X Business could provide thousands of dollars in travel value, making it worth a look for businesses with high spending needs. Let's look at the details and go over what you need to know before applying. Capital One Venture X Business current offer New Venture X Business applicants can earn up to 300,000 bonus miles and a $1,000 travel credit on the card after meeting two spending thresholds: - Earn 150,000 bonus miles after spending $40,000 on purchases in the first four months from account opening. - Earn an additional 150,000 bonus miles and a $1,000 Capital One Business Travel credit (to use in the first cardholder year) after spending $120,000 total on purchases in the first four months from account opening. Based on TPG's October 2026 valuations, the full offer is worth up to $6,550, including the $1,000 travel credit. While this isn't the highest bonus we've seen on the card, it's still a competitive offer that exceeds our recommended threshold for when to apply. To maximize the bonus, we recommend transferring your miles to one of Capital One's 15-plus airline and hotel partners. You also have the option to redeem your miles for a statement credit to cover travel expenses at a rate of 1 cent per mile. The Venture X Business carries a $395 annual fee, which is more than offset by a $300 annual Capital One Business Travel credit and anniversary bonus miles every year you hold the card. How does this compare to past Venture X Business offers? The highest offer we've seen in the card's history was for up to 400,000 bonus miles in November 2025, though it required spending $150,000 in six months to earn the full bonus. While the current offer falls short of that record, it's still above our recommended 150,000-mile threshold for when to apply. If your business can comfortably meet the spending requirements, this offer is worth considering. Why you should apply for the Capital One Venture X Business The Venture X Business has the same reasonable annual fee that so many love about the personal version, plus key benefits, including: - Anniversary bonus: Receive 10,000 miles each cardholder anniversary, worth $185 based on our valuations. - Annual travel credit: Receive an up to $300 annual credit for travel booked through Capital One Business Travel. - Global Entry/TSA PreCheck credit: Receive up to $120 in statement credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck. - Lounge access: Get unlimited access to Capital One lounges and Priority Pass lounges (where you can also bring up to two guests) worldwide. - Luxury hotel access: Access Capital One's Premier Collection and Lifestyle Collection programs for elite-like benefits when staying at participating hotels. Plus, when you spend on this card, you'll earn: - 10 miles per dollar spent on hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Business Travel - 5 miles per dollar spent on flights and vacation rentals booked through Capital One Business Travel - 2 miles per dollar spent on all other eligible purchases As mentioned above, the $395 annual fee is easily offset by the value of the annual travel credit and anniversary bonus, even before factoring in the welcome offer, lounge access and the card's earning potential. The Capital One Venture X Business is offering a valuable welcome bonus for business owners who can meet its substantial spending requirements. If your business can meet the spending requirements, this could be a good opportunity to earn a substantial stash of Capital One miles. However, businesses with lower expenses may be better off considering one of our other picks for the best business credit cards or the personal Capital One Venture X Rewards Credit Card.

item.title: This $19 App Helps You Cut Subscriptions You’ve Forgotten About
item.description:
Source: PCMag
TL;DR: Get lifetime access to the PocketWise Subscription Manager for just $19 (MSRP $59). It’s easy to lose track of how many subscriptions you’re paying for, especially when they renew on different dates. PocketWise Subscription Manager helps you organize recurring expenses, and lifetime access is just $19 (MSRP $59) for a limited time. Available for iOS and Android, PocketWise tracks unlimited subscriptions, including streaming services, memberships, apps, and recurring bills. It brings everything into one dashboard, showing what you spend monthly and annually. You can manually enter expenses, import bank statements using AI-assisted parsing, or add information through receipts, photos, and confirmation emails. Once everything is organized, PocketWise displays upcoming payments on a subscription calendar and sends renewal reminders before charges are due. Price history tracking also helps you identify increases you might otherwise overlook. Sharing subscriptions with roommates or family? PocketWise breaks down shared payments so you can see exactly how much you’re responsible for. The app also includes spending forecasts, customizable categories, multi-currency support, and data exports.

item.title: 4 slept-on Netflix original shows that are absolute must-watches
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek
Netflix puts out a pretty wide array of original shows, ranging from massively popular icons like Stranger Things to questionable and poorly rated shows like Hype House. Sometimes, though, Netflix puts out some brilliant masterpieces that don't quite reach mainstream popularity, instead garnering cult followings or, more sadly, fading slowly into obscurity. Despite missing the mainstream mark, the following shows have claimed a special place in my streaming rotation. They deserve much more attention than they originally got because of their fantastic stories, lovable characters, and beautiful art direction. From light-hearted comedies to bone-chilling horrors, there are many hidden gems on Netflix waiting to be discovered. The Residence, created by Paul William Davies, is a fairly new Netflix original. It debuted in March of 2025, and while it received positive reviews, it hasn't gotten nearly enough attention. It is a goofy whodunnit that fully embraces the fun of the genre while still feeling witty and clever at every turn. The murder mystery was captivating, and I ended up watching it from start to finish in one sitting. I can't believe that I had never heard of it before I gave it a shot earlier this year. On the night of an important state dinner in the White House, there is a murder. An eccentric yet brilliant detective with a penchant for birding, Cordelia Cupp (Uzo Aduba) is brought in to solve the mystery. Drama unfolds and everyone's dirty laundry is laid bare, with Cordelia's dry humor and sharp wit bringing about tons of laughs along the way. It is so hard to believe that this show didn't quite reach mainstream success. I'm always blown away at how few people I know have watched this show. Santa Clarita Diet strikes a balance between horror and comedy, taking a well-established genre and turning it on its head. After a three-season run, Netflix decided to cancel the series, citing low viewership as the reason. Its cancellation is tragic, not just because it was a fantastic show, but also because season three ended on a massive cliffhanger. Santa Clarita Diet stars Timothy Olyphant and Drew Barrymore as a married couple who both work as realtors in Santa Clarita. The world is turned upside down when Sheila (Drew Barrymore) dies and goes through a pretty dramatic transformation. While she feels better than ever, Sheila and her family are forced to deal with the wake of destruction that she leaves behind her. Raphael Bob-Waksberg is a renowned figure in the world of television, most acclaimed for creating the heart-wrenching animated series BoJack Horseman, alongside designer Lisa Hanawelt. In 2024, Bob-Waksberg announced Long Story Short, a dramedy that follows a Jewish family in a uniquely non-linear fashion, jumping back and forth between their childhood and adult lives. Despite a 100% score on Rotten Tomatoes, it hasn't been able to grab the mainstream quite like BoJack Horseman did. Bob Waksberg's animated comedy-drama features a star-studded cast, with names like Lisa Edelstein, Paul Reiser, Ben Feldman, and Max Greenfield, just to name a few. The story is gripping and relatable and explores the intricacies of a family filled with very different people. This is yet another show that sits in the shadow of some of its creator's other projects. Midnight Mass comes from the mind of Mike Flanagan, the man behind the brilliant and popular horror series, The Haunting of Hill House, and its spin-off, The Haunting of Bly Manor. Debuting in 2021, Midnight Mass stands alone, taking a different direction from Flanagan's other works. It might not have been nearly as popular as his other shows, but it is a must-watch for any horror fan. Rather than focusing on haunted houses, Midnight Mass focuses on other spooky supernatural beings. The show is about a priest, Father Paul Hill (Hamish Linklater), who arrives in a small town on an isolated island. The charismatic priest drives the town into a bit of a frenzy, winning over the townsfolk with seemingly impossible miracles. The town's lone sheriff, played by Rahul Kohli, slowly unfolds a dark plot behind Father Paul Hill's charismatic leadership. With Halloween just around the corner, this is a great show for getting the spooky vibes flowing. Popularity is not the only mark of a good show Netflix pushes its newest and most popular shows on you, meaning that some gems get hidden and forgotten. It even happens to some of Netflix's own original shows. The above are some of my personal favorites on the streaming platform, and while they might not have achieved mainstream success, I always recommend them to any friends and family willing to listen to my long-winded ranting.

item.title: Starlink Tips a Holiday Sales Push for Newest Dish Models
item.description:
Source: PCMag
Will a new Starlink dish arrive by the holiday season? A SpaceX executive is hinting that Starlink has been building up its inventory for a late-2026 subscriber-growth push. CFO Bret Johnsen subtly mentioned the strategy in SpaceX’s Q3 earnings call today. “We strategically managed our channel distribution to prioritize delivery of kits to retail channels ahead of the holiday season, which we expect will lead to increased activations in Q4,” he said. It’s a curious statement considering Starlink has been selectively selling the V5 dish on Starlink.com. In June, CEO Elon Musk also teased what appeared to be a next-gen Mini dish. The company is now discounting the first-gen Mini dish to $149 on Starlink.com, a sign it's trying to clear out the older inventory. Johnsen added that during the third quarter, the company “began ramping production of our V5 kits, which supported our progress on alleviating inventory constraints.” The statement suggests that the V5 model, which first arrived in July, was specifically designed to help SpaceX churn out more dish models at a faster rate, and possibly at a more cost-effective way. The V5 is currently available only on Starlink.com if you choose the lower-tier Residential 100 Mbps plan. The new dish model doesn’t offer a major speed boost over the older V4, but it’s smaller, lighter, and more power-efficient while delivering about the same performance. Third-party retailers have yet to start selling it in the US. There are signs that Starlink's growth might be stagnating. In its Q3 earnings report, SpaceX revealed that the number of consumer subscribers for Starlink reached 13.6 million globally during the period, up from 12 million in the previous quarter, “driven by growth in more developed markets,” Johnsen added. Still, the company added 1.6 million subscribers during the period, slightly lower than the 1.7 million it added from Q1 to Q2. That suggests Starlink’s subscriber growth can experience some “seasonality,” according to industry analyst Tim Farrar. In early August, the company revealed Starlink had 13 million-plus Starlink subscribers. “Striking to get 1M+ adds in first 6 weeks but only 0.6M in last 7 weeks,” Farrar noted. Hence, it’s possible Starlink saw higher growth in the summer months as people adopted it for outdoor use, but usage slowed in September as the school year resumed.

item.title: HyperX Cloud III S, Cloud Alpha 2, or CloudX Flight 2: Which Wireless Gaming Headset Is Right for You?
item.description:
Source: PCMag
Quick Answer: The HyperX CloudX Flight 2 Wireless (MSRP $139.99) is best suited for Xbox players, the HyperX Cloud III S Wireless (MSRP $179.99) is a strong choice for gamers who play across multiple platforms and devices, and the HyperX Cloud Alpha 2 Wireless (MSRP $299.99) is ideal for players who want simultaneous 2.4GHz and Bluetooth connectivity for gaming and secondary-device audio. A gaming headset is an essential piece of gear for in-game chatting and making sure you don’t miss any audio cues or dialogue. Finding the right headset isn’t just about looking at features and design; your gaming setup also plays a role. A headset designed for PS5 might not work at all with an Xbox, while other headsets can connect to multiple platforms. When shopping for a gaming headset, you need one that’s not just compatible with your gaming setup, but also just as fluid and versatile as the way you like to play. HyperX offers multiple Cloud headset options built for different priorities: the CloudX Flight 2 for primarily Xbox gamers, the Cloud III S Wireless for multi-platform gameplay, and the Cloud Alpha 2 for players juggling gaming with other devices and audio. Read on for a quick breakdown of these three headsets and find out which is right for your gaming needs. Which HyperX Wireless Headset Should I Get: CloudX Flight 2, Cloud III S, or Cloud Alpha 2? The headset you choose depends on your gaming style and preferences. If wireless Xbox connectivity is your priority, the CloudX Flight 2 is a great fit. If you tend to play across a wide variety of devices, the Cloud III S is a versatile option. And if simultaneous 2.4GHz and Bluetooth connectivity across multiple devices is important, go with the Cloud Alpha 2. The table below breaks down the price and capabilities for each option. Which HyperX Headset Works With Xbox, PS5, and PC? All three headsets are compatible with PC and PS5. The CloudX Flight 2 connects wirelessly to Xbox, while the Cloud Alpha 2 can only connect to Xbox with a cable. The Cloud III S is not compatible with Xbox. The CloudX Flight 2 is an official Xbox-licensed model, with an Xbox/PC mode switch built into its USB dongle. The headset is also compatible with PS5, PS4, Nintendo Switch, Mac, and mobile. The Cloud III S is compatible with PC, Mac, PS5, PS4, Nintendo Switch, and mobile devices and connects via 2.4GHz wireless, Bluetooth, or Instant Pair on select OMEN laptops. The Cloud Alpha 2 likewise wirelessly connects to PC, PS4, PS5, Switch, Mac, and mobile, in addition to the wired Xbox compatibility. How Long Does the Battery Really Last on Each HyperX Headset? Using an average of four hours of gameplay per day, HyperX’s rated battery life figures for the HyperX Cloud family range from weeks to around two months. Battery life will vary depending on the headset option, the connection type, and whether you use RGB lighting features. Here’s how the battery life for each model stacks up for everyday use: - For players who want RGB customization: CloudX Flight 2, with up to 20 hours on 2.4GHz or 23 hours on Bluetooth with its out-of-box lighting on; switching the lighting off extends those ratings to up to 100 and 150 hours - For gaming plus mobile use: Cloud III S, with up to 120 hours on 2.4GHz or up to 200 hours on Bluetooth - For fewer charging breaks: Cloud Alpha 2, with up to 250 hours on 2.4GHz or 125 hours with simultaneous 2.4GHz and Bluetooth How Do the Three Compare on Sound and Mic Features? All three headsets are built for gaming and voice chat, but each has its own strengths. The Cloud Alpha 2 uses multi-layer 53mm dual-chamber drivers with spatial audio through HyperX NGENUITY which provides spatial audio for a more immersive listening experience. The Cloud III S uses angled drivers to direct sound towards your ear canal to help audio sound crisp and clear. The CloudX Flight 2 has a built-in switch to quickly toggle between game audio and chat audio. Determining which headset to get based on sound and mics depends on what games you play and where. Here are a few guidelines to help you choose: - Xbox-first play with quick game or chat mixing: The CloudX Flight 2 features angled 50mm drivers, a detachable 10mm boom mic or built-in internal mic, and onboard audio mix and mic controls - Spatial audio across PC, PlayStation, Switch, and mobile: The Cloud III S comes with 53mm angled drivers and DTS Headphone:X spatial audio on PC - Finely tunable audio: The Cloud Alpha 2 has multi-layer 53mm dual-chamber drivers, spatial audio through HyperX NGENUITY software, a detachable 10mm boom mic, and an RGB base station with audio controls Across all three models, detachable boom mics can help capture everything you say to your teammates or enemies in voice chat more clearly. Are HyperX Headsets Comfortable for Long Gaming Sessions? The CloudX Flight 2, Cloud III S, and Cloud Alpha 2 are all designed for user comfort during short and extended gaming sessions. All three options weigh less than a pound and let you customize the fit to your head. That said, the materials and design details vary from headset to headset, so you’ll want to evaluate them based on your own comfort needs. The CloudX Flight 2 features memory foam ear pads and 90-degree rotating earcups that can better conform to your head. The Cloud III S offers another level of comfort for long-haul gaming sessions with a cushioned headband, memory foam ear cushions wrapped in premium leatherette, and an aluminum frame. It may be a fit for players who prefer a more padded fit when settling in for a full evening of back-to-back matches. Or, if your old headset leaves you feeling the heat (and not in a good way) after you’ve been locked into a game for two hours, the Cloud Alpha 2 uses breathable microfiber earpads that can help keep things cooler. The memory foam headband adds cushioning across the top of the head, and 90-degree rotating earcups give you a little more flexibility to adjust the fit. Shop the full Cloud headphone lineup at HyperX and pick up the pair that's right for you. What do you get with the HyperX Cloud Alpha 2 at $299.99 MSRP? The HyperX Cloud Alpha 2 offers up to 250 hours of play time on 2.4GHz or up to 125 hours with simultaneous 2.4GHz and Bluetooth, plus dual-chamber 53mm drivers, spatial audio, a customizable RGB base station, and a detachable boom mic. The box includes the headset, base station, detachable microphone, USB-C and USB-A cables, and a 3.5mm audio cable. Does the HyperX Cloud III S work with Xbox? No. The HyperX Cloud III S supports PC, PlayStation, Switch, Mac, and mobile, but not Xbox. For wireless Xbox support, look to the CloudX Flight 2, which is the official Xbox licensed model. Can the CloudX Flight 2 be used with a PS5 or PC? Yes. In addition to Xbox, the HyperX CloudX Flight 2 supports PC, PS5, PS4, Switch (docked mode), Mac, and mobile. Does RGB lighting affect battery life? Yes. The HyperX CloudX Flight 2 is rated for up to 100 hours on 2.4GHz or up to 150 hours on Bluetooth with lighting off, versus up to 20 or 23 hours, respectively, with its out-of-box RGB lighting on. Can I use these headsets with a cable? Only the HyperX Cloud Alpha 2 supports 3.5mm wired audio. The Cloud III S and CloudX Flight 2 use wireless audio connections; the Cloud III S also supports Instant Pair on select OMEN laptops. Can I take a phone call while gaming on a HyperX headset? Yes, the HyperX Cloud Alpha 2 supports simultaneous 2.4GHz and Bluetooth connections that let you game on one device while taking a call from another. The HyperX Cloud III S and CloudX Flight 2 allow you to switch between 2.4GHz and Bluetooth instead.

Still, it’s a great desktop piece that not only looks good, but has the power under the hood to back it up as well. What are good websites to find computer deals? There are a ton of sites that sell computers, and scouring through all of them would take you a lot of time—that’s why we do it for you here and highlight the best deals we find. However, to save you some time and frustration, you need to be smart about where you look at any given time of the year. If you’re looking for a new computer during the holidays or around popular sale periods such as Black Friday or back-to-school, then you are likely to find great deals directly through first party vendor websites. These include the retail storefronts of popular computer manufacturers such as HP, Dell, and Lenovo. However, if you are looking in between sales periods, it’s generally a good idea to search through large third-party retailers such as Amazon, Adorama, Walmart, BestBuy, and Newegg. Oftentimes these websites will offer limited Deals of the Day type sales in hopes of getting rid of excess stock. On the upside, you can score still-decent PCs at a steep discount. When’s the best time to shop for a PC computer? Typically you’ll want to time your PC computer shopping around a prominent sales period. The biggest sales periods are Black Friday/Cyber Monday in late November and Amazon Prime Day in early-to-mid July. The best sales often occur leading up to and during these two events and they are great times to snag a new PC computer for cheap. Other holiday shopping periods such as the New Year sales in January, President’s Day sales in February, and the back-to-school sales event in August are also good times to find discounts on computers. What type of desktop should I get? You’ll see a ton of options when searching for a desktop computer, but they all mainly fit into four main categories: productivity tower PCs, gaming PCs, mini PCS, and all-in-ones (AiO). Which you should end up buying is entirely dependent upon what your needs are and what you want to do with your computer. If you are looking for something that will work in a home office or family room, then a productivity PC or AiO with a solid CPU and lots of RAM and storage is probably the way to go. If gaming is your main concern, a gaming PC can offer a lot more bang for your buck than a laptop and you should focus on getting the best GPU possible. Or if you just want something that can fit anywhere and provide basic computing then a mini PC is a good bet. What CPU and GPU should I get? When looking at your new computer’s CPU, get at least an Intel Core i5 or AMD Ryzen 5, both of which will provide plenty of processing power for everyday computing tasks. If you don’t intend to do any PC gaming, then feel free to save some money by going with integrated graphics. However, if you are looking to get your game on, we recommend at least an Nvidia GeForce 3060 or AMD Radeon RX 6600 XT, as these are the least expensive discrete graphics cards that can handle ray tracing well. If you aren’t interested in those cutting-edge lighting effects, however, the RTX 3050 and Radeon RX 6600 also provide decent 1080p gaming performance at even lower prices. The RTX 5070 is a strong midrange card that will allow for high settings at 1440p while the RTX 5080 is capable of decent 4K gaming if that’s more your speed. For those who won’t compromise for anything besides the best, the RTX 5090 is really your only option currently. How much memory and storage does my PC need? As for RAM, we think its best to shoot for 16GB at the minimum for productivity and gaming, but for family computers and internet browsing, 8GB should suffice. Storage size is dependent upon your personal needs, but it is generally a good idea to opt for an SSD over an standard HDD as they are much faster and don’t significantly affect the price of a desktop. Before deciding, it’s best to consider what your intended use of the computer will be. Are you just doing work or web browsing? Then something like 512GB will be plenty. If you want to load up a lot of large files such as games or content creation projects, then you’ll need at least 1 or 2TB or storage. However, just remember that even if your computer doesn’t have enough storage built-in you can always upgrade your SSD or go with an external drive to increase your available storage options. Is it a good idea to buy a refurbished computer? Refurbished computers are used machines that have been repaired, upgraded, and cleaned for the purpose of reselling. They’re usually open-box returns, overstock, or models with minor cosmetic damage (scratches, scuffs, etc). Refurbished computers can be a bargain hunter’s dream as they’re likely still in good (or great) condition and you can save a lot of money. That being said, refurbished computers can have their downsides as well. In addition to cosmetic blemishes, some of the internal components might be a little older or outdated and they might not be in peak condition due to previous usage. If you do consider buying a refurbished computer I recommend looking at eBay as they offer a one-year warranty. You can also check out manufacturer’s retail storefronts like Dell’s Outlet Store and Apple’s Refurbished Store—just be sure to look at the terms of warranty offered before purchasing.

item.title: 12 unique vacation rentals you can book with points
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy
Hotel chains are increasingly incorporating boutique properties, nature lodges and other accommodations that go beyond the cookie-cutter expectations — without sacrificing the valuable benefits of loyalty programs. But what if you need more space to spread out while on vacation, or even want a full kitchen? Thankfully, some of our favorite hotel programs and credit card travel portals include vacation rentals — including some really interesting ones. From a historic airplane to a fairytale-worthy castle, here are 12 highly rated, undeniably cool vacation rentals where you can earn and burn points on a truly unique stay. Celebrate the Queen of Country with this fabulous Dolly Parton-inspired house, complete with pink guitar art, a "Nashville" marquee photo spot and a Grand Ole Opry-inspired karaoke stage. Dolly fanatics may never want to leave the building, but in case you do, it’s within easy walking distance of Centennial Park and the Parthenon. This four-bedroom dream house is a member of Homes & Villas by Marriott Bonvoy, so you (and up to 11 friends) can earn and burn points here. Nightly rates start around $525 or 105,000 Bonvoy points. For travelers seeking a relaxing retreat — and trying to reduce their environmental impact — you can’t beat this eco-conscious villa in the popular beach town of Tamarindo. It filters its own water to prevent the need for plastic bottles, recycles all wastewater and composts organic waste to feed the lush native garden surrounding it. With six bedrooms and five baths, up to 14 guests can stay here for a relaxing retreat. You can book a stay from $1,165 or 233,000 Marriott points per night. Oenophiles will love this sprawling estate, built in the 1880s and now part of Hyatt Homes & Hideaways. The fully stocked underground wine cellar is a highlight, but the drinks don’t end there. Guests will find themselves blocks away from the shops, restaurants and wineries of downtown Fredericksburg, the heart of Texas Hill Country’s celebrated wine scene. The Homestead is bookable through World of Hyatt, starting around $1,200 or 100,000 Hyatt points per night. It sleeps up to 18 guests across 11 bedrooms. If you’ve ever dreamed of staying inside a trullo — a conical-roofed stone hut found in Italy’s Puglia region — this is your chance to do it with points. Select Chase cardholders can redeem points through Chase Travel to book vacation rentals, including Oak & Trulli, a Plum Guide property in the Itria Valley. You’ll feel like you’ve stepped back in time as you meander through stone archways and dine al fresco on the private terrace. This two-bed, two-bath property can accommodate up to five guests and one dog. Prices start around $300 or 30,000 Ultimate Rewards points per night. For a true nature getaway, look no further than this cozy treehouse built from shipping containers on 55 acres of Michigan woodland. You can’t drive all the way to the treehouse; you must walk about 100 steps up a mulched path from the parking spot (don’t worry, snowshoes are provided in winter). With room for just two guests, it makes a perfect getaway for outdoorsy couples or solo travelers. You can book a stay starting from $430 or 86,000 Marriott points per night; there’s a two-night minimum stay. Step into your very own fairytale at this one-of-a-kind property in Banner Elk, North Carolina. From the antique church doors and 24-foot foyer ceiling to paneling imported from England and a real suit of armor, The Castle at Valle Cruces feels royal inside and out. That doesn’t mean you’ll experience medieval-level comfort, however. The castle is filled with modern amenities like a hot tub, workout area, game room, theater room and five fireplaces — all spread over 10,000-plus square feet of space. Nightly rates at this six-bedroom stunner start around $1,550 or 310,000 Marriott points. Aviation junkies can sleep in a piece of history in this 1941 WWII Douglas DC-3 Airliner, which has been converted into a one-bedroom, one-bath accommodation for up to four guests. The cockpit has been transformed into a fitness facility, with the control panel still intact, and the kitchen is illuminated by the original square portholes. Plus, a deck has been added over the wing so you can grill your dinner while enjoying the sights and sounds of the surrounding forest. This fascinating property in Deerbrook, Wisconsin is bookable on Vrbo, which is part of Expedia Group’s One Key loyalty program. Rates start around $400 per night, or you can pay for part or all of your stay with OneKeyCash. A trip to the Land of the Rising Sun wouldn’t be complete without a stay at a ryokan, or traditional Japanese inn. If you’re traveling with a large group (up to 16), you can get a similar experience while staying close together in this villa inspired by the machiya, or traditional Japanese townhouse. You’ll find Japanese touches throughout, from the low beds and dining set to a Japanese-style sauna, semi-open-air bath and outdoor garden. Beverages, including local sake, are all included in your stay. The villa is located in Nara, a popular tourist town near Kyoto and Osaka. Rates start around $1,075 or 215,000 Marriott points per night; there is a two-night minimum. If you’re planning a family or friends trip to Disneyworld Orlando, why not go all-out at this on-theme vacation rental? It’s just a half-hour drive from the parks, and several of its 10 bedrooms have fun themes such as Encanto, Star Wars and Harry Potter. And with a pool, video games and arcade games, guests will find no shortage of family fun. This World of Hyatt property has a four-night minimum stay, with rates starting from $515 or 43,000 points per night. For a uniquely rugged stay, look no further than this sun-drenched tiny house on a working alpaca farm in Windeyer, New South Wales. Guests can enjoy bushwalks, mountain biking and feeding the animals on the farm’s 300 acres, or venture further out for wineries and hot air ballooning. Though you can expect full bathroom facilities, some — like the waterless compost toilet — are on the more rugged (and eco-friendly) side. Each tiny house can accommodate up to four guests, but there are multiple units on the property, so you could potentially plan a larger group stay or family reunion. Nightly rates start at just $140 or 27,500 Marriott points. Since Capital One Travel offers vacation rentals as part of its Premier and Lifestyle collections, eligible cardholders can access elitelike perks while enjoying more space and a full kitchen. Fairway Oasis by Avant Stay has plenty of room and endless entertainment for up to 17 guests (and pets, too). There’s a speakeasy game room and sports bar, but the real highlight is the “ultimate backyard,” which features everything from a hot tub and fire pit to life-sized cup pong and pickleball. Rates start around $1,000 (and you’ll earn bonus points on your purchase) or 100,000 miles per night. Lord of the Rings fans and bookcationers will swoon at this cozy, points-friendly hobbit hole in Cosby, Tennessee. Beyond the unmistakable round doors and windows, every detail is carefully designed to fit the theme. Will you find the One Ring hidden somewhere on the property? There’s only one way to find out. You can book your two-night minimum stay from around $300 or 60,000 Marriott points per night. Vacation rentals don’t have to be dull; in some cases, the property alone is worth the trip. And since these 12 unforgettable properties are bookable through popular hotel programs and credit card platforms, you can redeem points for a stay or earn bonus points on a paid stay. On the other hand, if you find your dream stay isn’t bookable through one of these avenues, don’t forget you can still maximize your earnings on vacation rentals with the right credit card.

item.title: The Best Airbnbs in Turks and Caicos for Group Trips, Family Getaways, and Solo Adventures

Grace Bay may get most of the attention, with its luxury resorts, restaurants, and seemingly endless stretch of sand, but part of the appeal of Turks and Caicos is how quickly things quiet down once you leave it behind. For all its five-star resorts and enviable villas, Turks and Caicos can also be a wonderfully easy place to settle in and stay awhile at a vacation rental or Airbnb. Having your own space means leisurely mornings, sandy swimsuits tossed straight into the washing machine, and long lingering nights spent sipping a rum punch. And whether that home base is on Providenciales or one of the quieter islands beyond it, that extraordinary water is rarely far from view. Read on for my favorite vacation rentals and Airbnbs in Turks and Caicos for a Caribbean island escape you arenât soon to forget. FAQ: Where are the best places to stay in Turks and Caicos? For a first visit, Providenciales offers the greatest variety and the easiest access to restaurants, shopping, beaches, and activities. Grace Bay is the center of the action, while Turtle Cove and The Bight put you close to snorkeling and dining. Chalk Sound and Taylor Bay, on the other hand, are quieter choices farther from the resort strip. Travelers looking for more seclusion can head to North or Middle Caicos, where development is limited and beaches are far less crowded. Grand Turk boasts beautiful beaches alongside the historic streets of Cockburn Town, while private islands such as Parrot Cay offer a more exclusive resort experience. How long should you visit Turks and Caicos? Five to seven days is a good amount of time for most Turks and Caicos trips, particularly if you plan to stay primarily on Providenciales. That leaves enough time for several beach days along with snorkeling and boating excursions, and the ability to explore different parts of the island without overloading your itinerary. If you want to combine Providenciales with North or Middle Caicos, Grand Turk, or one of the private islands, consider a week or longer so the additional ferry or flight connections donât make the trip feel rushed.

item.title: The best UK vineyard stays to book for fine wine, rolling views and boutique design in 2026
item.description:

If, like most, when you think of a vineyard escape, your mind first drifts to the hills of Sicily, or the lavender fields of Provence, or perhaps a long lunch overlooking the mountains of the Western Cape, then you're not alone. As a London-based sommelier, I'm especially interested in what's happening on the local wine scene, and travelling the country to visit some of the best vineyards in the UK is part of my work. It's an industry that has evolved loudly and confidently over the past decade. While it may not always feel like we have much regional variation, especially with our climate, grapes are now successfully ripening in many parts of the UK, each offering its own distinctive terroir. English sparkling wines rightly continue to command global attention. However, our still wines have also been gaining international interest, from textured, chalky Pinot Noirs to elderflower-filled Bacchus and Rosés that evoke fruit in a revival of their French counterparts. Our UK wines have not only benefited from the warmer weather but also from vignerons being able to invest in better vineyard practices. Forward-thinking vineyards are now growing across the country from Cornwall to North Wales. This shift means you no longer need to board a plane to enjoy a wine-filled weekend, as a new era of homegrown wine travel is unfolding on our doorstep. You'll find hotels with Michelin-starred tasting menus, converted boutique barns, and winemakers eager to share not only their bottles but also their hospitality. Yes, what we have may not be the orange glow of terracotta roofs or the smell of Mediterranean shores, but what we have is something far more subtle, but arguably far more interesting, and sometimes a fair bit muddier. item.title: 9 best pizza places in Edinburgh for New York-style slices and charred Neapolitan creations
item.description:
Source: Condé Nast Traveler UK
If 36 years of loving something qualifies you as an expert, then let it be known that I know a thing or two about pizza. Hot, cold, delivered or dine-in, I’ll have it any way it comes, but preferably it’s fresh from a wood-fired oven, and the cheese pull is so long you have to twirl it round a little to force a break – but I’m really not fussy. Edinburgh might not be where you’d instinctively head for big old pizza pies, but Scotland’s capital city is doing a pretty stellar job at coming up with the goods. It’s a city full of great food, with its best restaurants a mix of independent fine diners and more casual spots ideal for weeknight dinners, and the pizzeria scene is no different to the wider set. I’ve been eating out in Edinburgh since I was a child, being taken as a treat by my parents when I was wee and slowly transitioning to treating myself as I made my way into adulthood. Now it’s a city I enjoy the spoils of weekly, wandering its streets in search of the very best bites. Below are my picks of tried and tested best pizza in Edinburgh I return to time after time when I find myself in need of a good slice. Ask most Edinburgh dwellers their favourite pizza spots, and I’m willing to bet nine times out of ten they’re going to say Razzo. This tiny spot on Leith Walk is perennially popular thanks to its molten, Neapolitan-style pizzas, which it fires out at speed to keep its constant stream of hungry diners well fed. I’m a firm believer in getting the basics right, and Razzo nails just that, combining hand-stretched dough with quality ingredients. The Marinara is an absolute classic, but if you prefer a more heavily loaded option then the mortadella combination, made with yellow tomatoes and burrata from Puglia is pretty special (as is the fried mozzarella sandwich as a starter, FYI). Razzo is a takeaway first and foremost, but there are a couple of tables you can book too. Address: Leith Street, Edinburgh EH1 3AU There’s nothing quite like a beautifully puffed-up, slightly charred crust on a pizza, and Dough excels at just that. These gorgeous creations are stone-baked for that authentic flavour, a light base and a crisp bottom, and come topped with all kinds of ingredients sourced from Italian suppliers, from San Marzano tomatoes to olives from Abruzzo. There are a couple of white base options, with my favourite coming topped with mini roast potatoes and smoked cheese for something that tastes like a midpoint between tartiflette and a carbonara. For any plant-based pals, there is also a whole vegan menu which doesn’t just give you the regular veggie options with the cheese removed, but instead offers thoughtful combinations, including a truffle mushroom number with vegan cheese. Address: 172 Rose Street, Edinburgh EH2 4BA If you value authenticity when it comes to your pizza, Matto does it best. The slowly fermented dough has a slight edge to it, and pizzas are cooked in a wood-fired oven for that signature smoky hum, which helped earn it the title of the best pizza in Scotland in 2024 at the Deliveroo Awards no less. While the technique might strictly adhere to age-old practices, the toppings are fun and ever-changing with the seasons, seen in combinations like a pumpkin cream base topped with mozzarella, friarielli, gorgonzola, fresh chilli and crispy fried leeks. Starters, salads and sides are all on tap too, if you fancy making a fuller feast of it, and there’s even a dessert pizza dripping with Nutella and pistachio creme for a pudding that will do its best to ignite some childhood joy in you. Address: 29-33 Newington Road, Edinburgh EH9 1QR There’s nothing quite like the experience of getting a Civerino's takeaway and sitting on the beach at Portobello looking out towards the sea, taking in the scene of families playing on the beach, owners walking their dogs and people mad enough to swim in the water, whatever the weather. This is a more American-style offering, with a thinly stretched base and toppings that go as close to the edge of possible, with a structure that is satisfyingly foldable. The team here also takes its quantities of cheese very seriously, which I appreciate, covering the crust in finely grated Parmesan for an extra flavour hit. For deep-pan lovers there’s also a Detroit option, with crisp edges and a doughy centre. The New York-style pizza toppings span classics like ham and mushrooms to twists on bold flavours like chicken schnitzel. Address: 47-49 Figgate Lane, Edinburgh EH15 1HJ For those who like their pizza Neapolitan-style, Pizza Posto is a reliable choice in the city centre. The dough is made with a blend of cereals and left to rise slowly for 24-48 hours before being cooked at high heat in clay ovens, giving the bases a soft, light texture and a good crust. The menu covers the classics, from a simple marinara to a margherita, alongside more substantial combinations for when you fancy something a little more indulgent. The Grande Italia, topped with Parma ham, burrata and rocket, is one for those who like their pizza piled high with good things. There are also white-based pizzas, calzones and dessert options, making this a good shout for a casual lunch or an easy-going dinner with a group. Address: 16 Nicolson Street, Edinburgh EH8 9DH If you’re after something a little different from the usual Neapolitan round, Pala is well worth seeking out. Specialising in Roman-style pizza al taglio, this Leith spot from the people behind Twelve Triangles (one of Edinburgh’s best bakeries) serves pizza by the slice, baked until crisp and cut to order. The format makes it ideal for a quick bite, or for picking up a couple of different slices if you can’t settle on just one topping. The menu includes combinations such as potato, pecorino and sun-dried tomato pesto, alongside courgette, feta and roasted cherry tomato for a veggie-friendly option. There are meatier choices, too, including salame piccante with friarielli and ricotta. Add a slice of tiramisu to finish, and you’ve got a rather lovely little pizza stop. It’s worth checking the opening hours before heading over, as the shop operates on selected days of the week. Address: 7 Jane Street, Edinburgh EH6 5HE Leith has no shortage of good pizza (or good restaurants, as demonstrated here), and San Ciro’s is another name to have on your radar. This neighbourhood pizzeria on Leith Walk welcomes diners for a relaxed Italian meal, with pizza at the heart of the offering. It’s a good option if you’re looking to make an evening of it rather than simply grabbing a takeaway, with a menu that also includes drinks and other Italian favourites. The restaurant has a laid-back feel that suits a catch-up with friends or a casual midweek dinner, and its location makes it an easy stop if you’re exploring Leith on foot. Address: 148–150 Leith Walk, Edinburgh EH6 5DT Sometimes, what you really want is a big old slice of New York-style pizza, and that’s where Sear’s comes in. With its American-inspired approach, this is a good alternative to the city’s many Neapolitan pizzerias, particularly if you’re in the mood for a larger pizza to share or a generous solo slice with plenty of toppings. Sear’s offers 18-inch pizzas for pre-order and collection, making it a handy option for a night in, but its bread and butter lies in its single serves which are heated up on request for diners looking for a quick bite. There are a few high stools gathered around the edges of this trendy joint, but most people choose to take away their spoils on paper plates and enjoy their feed sitting outside the shop or on the grass in The Meadows nearby. A tomato slice starts at £2, while you can get any slice and a soda for £5.50. Not bad in this economy. Address: 27A Marchmont Road, Edinburgh EH9 1HY For a taste of Naples without leaving Edinburgh, Pizzeria 1926 is a strong contender. The restaurant has been serving Neapolitan pizza in the city since 2016, and its traditional approach puts the focus firmly on quality ingredients and that unmistakable soft, chewy crust. It’s also a member of the Associazione Verace Pizza Napoletana, an organisation dedicated to preserving the traditions of authentic Neapolitan pizza. The atmosphere is laid-back, making it a good choice for a relaxed sit-down meal. It’s also just a short walk from Haymarket station, which makes it easy to reach if you’re coming from out of town. Top picks include a four cheese with honey and hazelnuts and a loaded meat-lover's dream made with salami, meatballs and sausage. Address: 85 Dalry Road, Edinburgh EH11 2AA

item.title: 11 best bars in Hong Kong for masterful mixology
item.description:
Source: Condé Nast Traveler UK
Having lived in Hong Kong for almost two decades, I’ve seen the city’s nightlife in many guises – a fresh-eyed arrival partying into the midnight hours, a lifestyle writer hunting down the hottest new openings, a long-time resident with my favourite regular hangs, and a constant tour guide to visiting friends, showing off the city’s best. As the years have passed, my tastes have somewhat evolved (the less said about those vodka shots in a Russian bar’s ice room, the better) alongside the city’s bar scene itself – and the crowning of our hometown hero, Bar Leone, as the winner of World’s 50 Best Bars for the second year running, aptly reflects the purple patch we’re currently in. These days, you no longer need to choose between amazing drinks, food or vibes; the top bars here offer all the above and then some, with creativity and chutzpah to spare. Narrowing down my best bars in Hong Kong is no mean feat – but these are the ones that my friends and I find ourselves hankering to return to the most, a cross-section of the diversity on offer, where I’d always be happy to sink back a bevvie (mostly non-alcoholic nowadays!), take a tourist or simply soak up some vibes. Cheers to that. A roaring success that’s worth the hype – and the inevitable wait for a table. Twice anointed the title of World’s Best Bar, this unpretentious spot helmed by Italian Lorenzo Antinori was built around the idea of “cocktail popolari”, aka cocktails for the people. Inspired by traditional neighbourhood bars in Rome, the vibes are immaculate: warm, laidback and approachable, even after all the accolades. Drinks are well-balanced, minimal and the antithesis to style over substance – seasonal Negronis and iced teas, a velvety Olive Oil Sour, an umami-loaded Filthy Martini. Cancel the dinner reservation; their smoked olives and mortadella-laden focaccia are also nothing short of legendary. Sleek, stylish, sophisticated. Quiet confidence is very much the order of the day at Mius, the buzzy neighbourhood bar helmed by native Hong Konger Shelley Tai – and her “simple things done right” ethos is showcased in every element, from the invitingly elegant mid-century design to a drinks menu defined by modern classics, sometimes done straight up (a crisp, clean Highball), other times with a refined twist (a Strawberry Negroni that effortlessly straddles the line between sweet and bitter). Order comfort food plates like vodka rigatoni and beef sukiyaki toast and you’re set for the night. Paying homage to the past while firmly looking toward the future; Kinsman strikes the perfect balance between golden-hued nostalgia and 21st-century cool, spearheaded by co-founder Gavin Yeung’s championing of once-overlooked indigenous Chinese spirits. Drinks here are bold, quirkily inventive and unlike anything you’ll find elsewhere – Milk & Honey features yuk bing siu, a rice wine macerated with pork fat, while other creations are inspired by historic Chinatowns; shout-out too for their well-judged non-alcoholic selection (the taro-coconut Orh Nee 2.0 tastes like dessert in mocktail form, without tipping into oversweet territory). Don’t sleep on the food either, which proffers a fresh spin on Cantonese classics, including a supersized prawn toast made with smoked pork lard. You don’t top Asia’s 50 Best Bars list for three years running without knowing a thing or two about great drinks. Inspired by the Mexican drinking dens frequented by founder Jay Khan during his travels, COA is a celebration of all things agave – with a 41-page agave spirit-dedicated menu that delves deeper into varieties, terroirs and producers. Tequila and mezcal get their chance to shine on the tightly curated cocktail list, which spotlights Mexican flavours and seasonal ingredients, with new concoctions debuting weekly. Cosy and intimate, this is a temple of knowledge that wears its expertise lightly. Address: Shop A, LG/F, Wah Shin House, 6-10 Shin Hing Street, Central While plenty of bars Kowloon-side offer ringside seats to Hong Kong’s spectacular harbour views, not many do so with the elan of DarkSide. This refined cocktail parlour in the uber-glam Rosewood Hong Kong hotel delivers innovative cocktails inspired by Kowloon’s heritage, alongside an extensive library of dark spirits like rum, calvados and whiskey – including an exclusive house-crafted cognac blend. It feels only right that this sophisticated selection comes soundtracked by sultry live jazz into the midnight hours – plus those all-important glittering vistas really do their best work at night. Address: 2/F, Rosewood Hong Kong, Victoria Dockside, 18 Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui Happening upon a hidden door, feeling like you’re in on a particularly dishy secret – there’s just something special about a speakeasy and The Green Door is one of Hong Kong’s best. Nestled amid the stalls of Graham Street wet market, this underground hideaway is inspired by Alice in Wonderland, with sweeping curved arches and cushy leather banquettes. The drinks offer playful takes on classics while the all-American apple pie, served with lashing of golden caramel, has its own fan club. Address: LG/F, Welley Building, 97 Wellington Street, Central When the weather gods are smiling, nothing hits quite like a cheeky sundowner on Terrible Baby’s leafy rooftop terrace. Located bang in the midst of Jordan’s urban sprawl at the artsy Eaton hotel, Terrible Baby boasts a hip laidback vibe, with idiosyncratic cocktails to match – try Dong Ling Cha, their rum-based remix of a quintessentially Hong Kong iced lemon tea. Live music sets, customisable shisha blends and pup-spotting opportunities add further to the fun. Address: 4/F, Eaton Hong Kong, 380 Nathan Road, Jordan Precision begets perfection; that’s the philosophy at Gokan, the first Hong Kong venture from renowned Japanese mixologist Shingo Gokan – resulting in ingenious drinks like Watermelon Koffeez, which transforms gin, clarified watermelon juice and lightly roasted coffee into something far more magical than the sum of its parts. With the word “gokan” also playing on the Japanese for “five senses”, the drinks menu is arranged into the five fundamental flavours (sweet, spicy, sour, bitter and savoury), with each available as a highball, on the rocks or strained. The substantial food menu complements affairs perfectly – and yes, it too is divided into five sections, spanning everything from hearty claypot rice to a fruit-filled kakigori shaved ice dessert. In a city that often feels like it’s chasing the next big thing, a venue lasting over 30 years must be doing something right. Once you try The Globe, a down-to-earth gastropub, you’ll know exactly why it’s endured – an expansive craft beer selection, including ever-changing guest taps and dozens of hand-picked local brews; a banging food menu, starring their signature plate-sized pies (vote for the monthly special via their Instagram) and a top-notch Sunday roast; and an unassuming, relaxed ambience that makes the place feel like home. The local we all wish we had. Address: Garley Building, 45-53 Graham Street, Central With most of Hong Kong’s buzziest bars located a stone’s throw from each other in Central, the city’s CBD, finding something special further afield feels all the more exciting. BOUND is a defiantly low-fi, indie joint that has become a much-loved stalwart of Kowloon’s flourishing creative scene; part coffee shop, part eatery, part bar – all executed with flair. Expect local bands, funky pop-ups and playlists you’ll be saving for the journey home, served alongside a nifty selection of interest-piquing cocktails and natural wines. Address: 32 Boundary Street, Prince Edward Hong Kong just can’t get enough of Lorenzo Antinori – and the brains behind Bar Leone has struck gold again with his next project, Montana. Channelling Cuba’s golden age of cocktails by way of 1970s Miami grooves, Montana is heaps of fun, with drinks that boast just as much mojo as the pulsating salsa-disco soundtrack. The Montana Daiquiri is based on an original 1930s Cuban recipe, while the Pina Colada features juicy pineapple barbequed there and then behind the bar.

item.title: Best ice skating in London this winter: 8 of the most festive spots
item.description:
Source: Condé Nast Traveler UK
Among the countless festive activities the city offers, enjoying ice skating in London at one of its most beautiful rinks is truly unmissable. I blame this entirely on cheesy Christmas films, but there are few things that get me into the Christmas spirit quite like it. Every year, I convince myself that it can't actually be that difficult and that I definitely look graceful while trying to keep myself from falling – but, alas, I usually end up spending most of my time sitting on the ice. Although I'm unlikely to ever win an ice skating competition, wrapping up in my warmest coat, putting on a pair of skates and attempting to glide across the ice always makes me happy and puts me in a festive mood. There are several things that make this even better. First: having a spectacular Christmas tree in the background and second: a steaming cup of hot chocolate waiting for me when I finally reach the exit. And while I'm always tempted by a cosy winter holiday in the UK or a stay in one of the country's most beautiful hotels for Christmas, nowhere beats London during the festive season. Every autumn, some of London’s most beautiful landmarks transform into spectacular outdoor ice rinks, making ice skating in London one of the loveliest ways to celebrate the arrival of the cold winter days. From the magnificent courtyard of Somerset House to the historic surroundings of Hampton Court Palace and the enormous Winter Wonderland ice rink in Hyde Park, there are plenty of places to practise your pirouettes (or simply try to stay upright). Whether you're planning a romantic date, a festive afternoon with friends or a family outing with little ones, the best ice rinks in London have something for everyone. Of course, ice skating in London isn't just for Christmas. The capital is also home to several year-round ice rinks, including Alexandra Palace, Streatham Ice Rink and Lee Valley Ice Centre, where you can enjoy indoor skating, learn to skate with professional coaches or even watch a game of ice hockey. But it's the seasonal outdoor rinks, with their twinkling lights, festive music and irresistible Christmas atmosphere, that make winter skating a particularly special activity. So, whether you're staying in London this December or planning a festive city break before heading somewhere warmer for some winter sun, these are the best places to go ice skating in London in 2026. Where is the best place to ice skate in London? London has plenty of beautiful ice skating rinks to choose from during the festive season. For a truly magical setting, Skate at Somerset House is one of the best places for ice skating in London, with its spectacular courtyard and 40-foot Christmas tree. Hampton Court Palace is another favourite, offering the chance to skate against the backdrop of Henry VIII's former home, while Battersea Power Station's riverside rink is perfect for those looking for something a little different. For a more traditional Christmas experience, head to Winter Wonderland in Hyde Park. How much does it cost to go ice skating in London? The cost of ice skating in London varies depending on the rink, time of day and date you visit. Generally, tickets for seasonal outdoor ice rinks start at around £10-£15 per person, although prices can rise to £20-£25 or more during peak periods, particularly at weekends and closer to Christmas. Skate hire is often included in the ticket price, but it's always worth checking before booking. For cheaper ice skating in London, look out for off-peak sessions during weekday mornings and afternoons. Skate in the shadow of a Tudor palace this winter as Hampton Court Palace's ice rink returns. Admire the regal beauty of the palace from every angle while gliding in the footsteps of some of England’s most famous Kings and Queens before refuelling at the newly designed café and bar. Inspired by King William III’s historic Orangery at Hampton Court Palace, the sparkling new area combines wood, lights and lush greenery to create a dazzling winter retreat. Watching on while pals take to the ice? Sip on a mulled wine or hot toddy from the award-winning Department of Coffee & Social Affairs and see the not-so-elegant tumbles play out. Address: Hampton Court Palace, Hampton Court Way, Molesey, East Molesey KT8 9AU Website: hamptoncourtpalaceicerink.co.uk Dates: 20 November 2026 - 3 January 2027 We know, we know: it's not the chicest recommendation. But Winter Wonderland is home to the UK's largest open-air ice rink, so if you're looking for garish festive excitement, this is the place for you. Glittering fairy lights and appearances from live musicians on the bandstand add to the festive atmosphere, while future pros get their first taste of the ice thanks to penguin aids designed for little ones. Book a session and enjoy all the fun of the fair before securing those blades, as some of the largest travelling funfair rides pop up. Feast on street food favourites, sip boozy hot chocolates, roam with indulgent toffee apples, or peruse the German market stalls littered across the park for some last-minute stocking fillers. Address: Hyde Park Winter Wonderland, Hyde Park, London W2 2UH Dates: 19 November 2026 - 3 January 2027 Alexandra Palace's ice rink is unique in that it's open year-round. Hundreds of thousands of skaters, from graceful professionals to not-so-graceful first-timers, take to the ice each year. Learn how to master the art of ice skating and turn it into a hobby with a course or private tuition, or just pop along for a thrilling themed evening. Once you’re done, tuck into mince pies or nurse a Baileys hot chocolate in the Festive East Court Café. Address: Alexandra Palace, Alexandra Palace Way, London N22 7AY Dates: Festive skates, 9 December 2026 - 4 January 2027 Gliding atop the shimmery ice in the shadow of Somerset House has become a tradition for Londoners in recent years. Between November and January, the courtyard transforms into a glorious festive destination, where music echoes off the neoclassical wings and onlookers sip steaming drinks while taking in the action from a distance. Virgin Atlantic Holidays brings its signature touches to the festivities for 2026 with a lounge-inspired Clubhouse with rink-side views, and the Chalet by Jimmy Garcia returns for indulgent helpings of signature raclette. For those who prefer a livelier atmosphere, the popular Skate Lates with Aperol Spritz are also returning this year, transforming the rink into an open-air party with DJ sets on selected evenings. Taking place on Wednesdays, Thursdays and Fridays from 8pm, the programme features an exciting line-up of DJs and music collectives, including Netil Radio, Daytimers, BUMPAH and Gauchoworld. After skating, visitors can enjoy an Aperol Spritz while soaking up the festive atmosphere and music. K-pop fans can also look forward to a special K-pop Party on 23 November, organised in collaboration with the Korean Cultural Centre UK, with DJ EMKAY playing everything from BTS and BLACKPINK hits to the latest K-pop tracks while skaters take to the ice. Address: Skate at Somerset House, Strand, London WC2R 1LA Dates: 11 November 2026 - 10 January 2027 Looking for an excuse to check out the Battersea Power Station mega-development? Their winter addition, Glide, may be just that. Three interconnecting rinks come together around a gargantuan Christmas tree in the centre, bringing them all together. Also returning this year is the 200-metre riverside skate trail, offering skaters the chance to glide along the Thames while taking in spectacular views of the London skyline. Post-skate, rest wobbly legs at The Glass House over a steaming hot chocolate or punchy cocktail and watch the next group take to the ice. There’s fun for all the family away from the ice thanks to a host of exciting new additions to the area in recent years. Gordon Ramsay’s casual pizza concept sits alongside Cinnamon Kitchen, one of the tastiest Indian restaurants in London, offering wholesome multi-course dining, while bars and shopping opportunities are plentiful. Address: Battersea Power Station, Circus Road West, Nine Elms, London SW11 8EZ Website: glidebatterseapowerstation.co.uk Leicester Square welcomes its second-ever ice rink for 2026, offering Londoners a skate among the hustle and bustle of the West End. Underbelly’s unique Christmas experience sees the square illuminated by sparkling lights in the evening, as music plays and skaters of all abilities and ages are invited to get involved. The circular rink surrounds the square's famous Shakespeare statue, with Christmas market stalls selling festive gifts and treats nearby. Once you've finished skating, head to the seasonal bar for a steaming hot chocolate, mulled wine or something a little stronger. Younger visitors can also make use of skate aids, while skate hire is included in the ticket price. As London’s only ice rink offering skating sessions that start every 15 minutes, it’s a great one for flexible itineraries. Address: Leicester Square, London WC2H 7LU There’s a solid argument for Queen’s House presenting the prettiest ice rink in London throughout the winter season. Glide around the heart of the stunning Greenwich UNESCO World Heritage Site, taking things as speedy or slow as you like thanks to a ‘skate-off pit lane’ for mid-session breaks, and recover in Zero Degrees restaurant over warming favourites. For 2026, the rink has doubled in size while keeping the same capacity, meaning more space to practise your moves without bumping into fellow skaters. There's also a programme of themed evenings, quiet skating sessions and special offers, including discounted tickets for students and free skating for children during selected sessions. Address: The Queen's House Ice Rink, Romney Road, London SE10 9NF Dates: 18 November 2026 - 3 January 2027 If you're planning a Christmas shopping trip, why not combine it with a little ice skating? Returning to Brent Cross Shopping Centre in North London for the 2026 festive season, On Ice brings a touch of Christmas magic to the area outside John Lewis, with a spacious outdoor rink illuminated by festive lights. Suitable for skaters of all abilities, the rink offers 45-minute sessions, with ice marshals on hand to help beginners find their feet and penguin-shaped skate aids available for younger visitors. Once you've finished skating, head inside the shopping centre to warm up with a hot chocolate, grab a bite to eat or get some Christmas shopping done. Tickets start at £13 for children and £15 for adults, including skate hire, and there's free parking for those arriving by car. Address: Brent Cross Shopping Centre, Prince Charles Drive, London NW4 3FP
